column1: # sm_120 (consumer Blackwell) memory-op load-use latency, per space and cache tier.
# Companion to memory_latency.tsv (sm_89).  Same method: single-warp clock64
# pointer-chase in which each memory op's address is a strict data dependency on
# the prior op's loaded value, so the SM cannot hide the latency behind ILP and
# the per-op cycle count IS the load-use latency.  clock64 counts SM cycles, so
# the figures are boost-clock invariant.  Each value is stable to +/-1 cycle
# across repeated launches; every chase is warmed before the timed pass.
# Part.  NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, sm_120, 188 SMs,
# 2430 MHz, 512-bit GDDR7 (~1598 GB/s theoretical, 1535 GB/s measured stream),
# L2 = 128 MiB, max shared memory 100 KiB/SM.  CUDA 13.2 (ptxas V13.2.86),
# Tier isolation.  The L1/shared array is unified and its split is a per-kernel
# carveout, so "L1_hit" is measured with no dynamic shared memory requested
# (L1-preferring carveout) and an 8 KiB working set.  L2 = 4 MiB set (overflows
# L1, far inside the 128 MiB L2; warmed twice before timing, since a cold 4 MiB
# set reads at DRAM latency).  DRAM = 512 MiB set.
# Caveat on STG.  The sm_89 table's STG row measures store-to-load FORWARDING
# (~7 cycles, the store hits L1 and forwards).  The sm_120 row here uses a
# volatile store/load pair, which defeats forwarding and measures a real
# write-then-read round trip -- a different quantity.  The two STG numbers are
# NOT comparable across the two files.
# UBLKCP is the TMA bulk-copy round trip (arrive.expect_tx -> cp.async.bulk ->
# mbarrier try_wait spin) for a 4 KiB tile issued by one elected lane.  It has no
# sm_89 counterpart: sm_89 has no TMA engine.  Both it and LDGSTS are full
# issue-to-completion round trips measured with nothing else in flight; under a
# warp-specialized producer/consumer pipeline ~97% of this latency is hidden
# behind concurrent math (see the overlap note below).
# Overlap.  With one producer warp issuing TMA and seven consumer warps running a
# dependent FMA chain, adding 0.143 ms of standalone TMA traffic costs 0.004 ms of
# wall clock -- 97% of the transfer is absorbed.  Overlap efficiency falls as the
# kernel becomes math-light (~69% when the math side is 0.08 ms).
